name: Santorini
summary: Treat the island as a collection of villages, beaches and archaeological sites rather than one sunset queue. Reserve one caldera day and one south-island day.
seasonNote: Summer is crowded and exposed walks are hot; winter transport and business hours are reduced. Check current local access notices.
arrival: The airport and ferry port require separate transfer plans; prearrange a late arrival or luggage-heavy transfer.
gettingAround: Buses radiate from Fira; taxis and transfers need budgeting. Long caldera walks are not suitable for luggage moves.
cashTip: Carry small EUR notes for bus fares and smaller vendors; peak-season transfers can add materially to spending.
foodTip: Try tomato fritters, fava and seafood; ask whether fish is priced by weight.
buyTip: Look for local ceramics and packaged island foods; compare caldera-front prices with inland shops.
baseArea: Fira for connections; Imerovigli for quieter caldera views

connections.note: About 1 hour airborne; ferries take several hours and may be disrupted by wind.
